**Palm et al., 2020** refers to a pivotal meta-analysis published in 2020 that evaluates the clinical impact of structured patient education on individuals with atrial fibrillation. Within the context of the Danish national quality development report *Atrieflimren i Danmark* (AFDK) by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), this publication serves as the primary evidentiary foundation for Indicator 8, which tracks and mandates structured [[patientuddannelse|Patientuddannelse]] (patient education) [^src1]. 

The study is critical for justifying patient-centered education as a core component of evidence-based cardiovascular care, aligning with both the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines and the Danish National Clinical Guidelines. By integrating patient education into the broader ABC Pathway treatment model, the research supports systematic quality development and clinical measurement in the Danish healthcare system [^src1].

Methodologically, the meta-analysis synthesized data from five randomized controlled trials and one non-randomized intervention study, encompassing a total of 2,007 patients [^src1]. It demonstrated a statistically significant 22% reduction in the combined endpoint of death and hospital readmission for the intervention group that received patient education compared to the control group that received no such education (Risk Ratio 0.78, 95% CI 0.63–0.97) [^src1]. These findings directly link educational interventions to tangible, life-saving clinical outcomes.
